data.title: Why Fox Can Finally Breathe a Sigh of Relief With the Roku Deal-and Why the NFL Can't — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Fox Corp.'s $22 billion acquisition of Roku will enhance how the media titan delivers its programming directly to viewers, a huge plus for livestreaming — especially its Sunday NFL games.

The deal, approved by Fox and Roku shareholders this week and expected to close early next year, essentially takes the risk off the table that the NFL will renew its 10-year contract with Fox early. The contract runs through 2033, but has an opt-out clause that either party can exercise after the 2029 season.

An early renewal has weighed on Wall Street — billions spent on traditional TV, the NFL's right to move high-profile games to powerful platforms like Amazon, and NFL's massive media rights that just keep going up.

And all of these things without new ways for Fox to make money.

Nailing down the deal, though, has analysts singing a different tune because of Roku's streaming operating system on TVs and revenue from ads and subscription fees for other streamer such as Netflix and Comcast's Peacock.

On Friday, Bank of America's Jessica Reif Ehrlich double upgraded Fox to Buy from Underperform and raised her price target to $85 from $54. The change sent shares 0.2% higher to $64.11 on Friday.

"One billion reasons to love the Roku deal," Ehrlich wrote, adding that the acquisition "changes the equation" for Fox stock.

Ehrlich said the early renewal risk and Fox's long-term positioning in streaming were behind her Underperform rating.

"With the risk of a near term NFL renewal largely receding until the 2029 opt-out window, the Roku acquisition fundamentally changes the strategic and financial narrative," she said.

Roku provides Fox with a credible path to transition toward a direct-to-consumer model, which has been a weakness for the company, Ehrlich said.

It also adds to Fox's current direct-to-consumer product, FOX One.

"One of the core bear arguments on Fox has been that the company...lacked a robust direct-to-consumer strategy to fully capture the migration of audiences and advertising budgets away from traditional pay-TV," she said. "Roku addresses this existential question," she added.

On Wall Street, Fox has an average Buy rating with a price target of $77.75, according to FactSet. The stock has six Buy ratings, seven Hold ratings, and one Sell rating.

Fox and Barron's parent News Corp share common ownership.

Write to Kit Norton at kit.norton@barrons.com

data.title: US arms firm Anduril could make interceptors in Europe, executive says
data.description:
US defence firm Anduril could eventually manufacture its newly unveiled Steelfin interceptor missiles in Europe, a company executive said this week, as governments aim to expand air-defence production after global conflicts highlighted shortages of interceptor missiles.

"I certainly hope that something like Steelfin could become a capability that we engage with both the Polish customer and industry," Brian Moran, Anduril's vice president for Europe, told Reuters on Monday.

"We would definitely consider engaging European partners and customers on this capability." Steelfin is due to undergo flight testing in 2027, according to Anduril.

Wars in Ukraine and the Gulf have strained stocks of air-defence interceptor missiles and caused delivery delays.

Moran said Anduril saw Steelfin as a complementary system that could provide a more affordable interceptor alongside existing missile-defence systems like the Patriot and others.

The company is already in talks to establish production in Poland of its Barracuda-500 cruise missile, and Moran said that experience could open the door to additional manufacturing projects.

"We're having a very good experience with our industry partner here, PGZ," he said, adding that discussions were also under way with the defence ministry and other government agencies. PGZ is Poland's state-owned arms group.

Poland, one of NATO's top defence spenders relative to the size of its economy, is seeking to expand domestic arms production and reduce reliance on foreign suppliers.

Moran said talks with PGZ, its WZL-2 unit and the government were focused on balancing local production with delivery speed and Poland's specific military requirements.

Asked about growing calls in Europe for defence-industrial sovereignty, Moran said the term could mean different things, from security of supply and maintenance capabilities to control over software upgrades and future modifications.

"Sovereignty has a cost. There's a cost to localisation. There's cost in terms of timing and just schedule. And those need to be considered in light of the threats that Europe collectively is facing."

While governments also want economic benefits from defence spending, the military outcome is most important, he said, adding that greater localisation can come with additional costs and longer timelines.

data.title: Dollar heads for weekly loss as Fed hike bets fade, AI jitters linger
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar set for first weekly loss after a month of gains
  • Investors scale back Fed hike bets despite hot inflation data
  • Tech selloff also weighing on dollar

By Laura Matthews

The dollar was lower on Friday and on track for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, reflecting fading expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike and lingering concerns about an AI-driven equity selloff.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer price readings initially rattled markets this week, but comments from Fed officials signaling no urgency to tighten policy further helped stabilize Treasury yields and eroded support for the dollar.

AI stocks fell sharply this week and the stress spread to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded into bets all along the supply chain worry data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts.

"What I found most interesting today and more broadly this week, is how closely the dollar has been tied to the AI trade," said Matt Weller, global head of market research at StoneX in Michigan. "Usually if we see a sell off in tech stocks you would expect the greenback to get a safe-haven bid. We are seeing an element of that into bonds, but the dollar is actually falling."

The dollar index , which measures it against six major peers, fell 0.17% to 101.87 and was set for a 0.35% weekly drop.

The pound and the Swiss franc led gains against the dollar this week, with the latter buoyed by safe-haven demand and expectations that even in a lower-rates environment Switzerland is unlikely to cut policy rates below the current zero level.

Sterling rose 0.31% to $1.3314 and was up 0.63% on the week, while the dollar fell 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246, leaving it down 0.67% for the week. The franc has gained more than 1.4% in the last two sessions.

Markets assign an 83% probability to the Fed keeping rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month earlier, the CME FedWatch Tool shows.

At the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "prejudge meetings."

"I don’t think there is enough support in (the) committee, particularly from the governors, for a rate hike in October. It still leaves December an unanswered question and there is a lot to happen between now and then," said John Velis, Americas macro strategist at BNY in New York.

EURO AREA FISCAL RISKS STILL IN FOCUS

Fiscal risks in France remained in the background after the jump in the French debt risk premium in early October.

The euro was last up 0.08% to $1.1227 after climbing 0.56% on Thursday in its biggest daily rise in two months, putting it on track for a 0.23% weekly gain.

Investors expect US President Donald Trump to steer clear of any escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a broader conflict could hurt his standing ahead of midterm elections by fuelling inflation.

Against the yen the dollar slipped 0.08% to 158.11, leaving the Japanese currency on track for a 0.13% weekly rise after dropping for four consecutive weeks as the Iran conflict supported the greenback.

Higher oil prices recently have been boosting the dollar while weighing on the currencies of energy-importing countries, such as those tied to the euro and yen.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday reiterated the risks of underlying inflation overshooting the central bank's 2% target.

data.title: How Weight-Loss Drugs Could Drive Victoria's Secret's Next Chapter — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Victoria's Secret stock has been riding high on a company turnaround, and a Wall Street firm thinks GLP-1s could offer a fresh tailwind — even if management hasn't spotted the impact yet.

Needham analyst Tom Nikic initiated coverage of the lingerie retailer on Friday with a Buy rating and $106 price target, betting on long-term upside from the weight-loss drug trend.

"As consumers' body types change, they may need to trade down into smaller sizes, and they might want to buy clothing that makes them feel 'sexier,' which could potentially drive them towards Victoria's Secret," he wrote in a note.

CEO Hillary Super said in an earnings call in June that while GLP-1 adoption has had a "minimal impact" on sales so far, the company will continue to monitor the trend.

Nikic added that Victoria's Secret is in the early stages of a "compelling" multi-year turnaround, which began when Super took the helm on Sept. 9, 2024. Since that day, the stock has risen about 284%, and is up 63% this year. As the company has continued to pull back its promotions and progress with its transformation, Nikic sees a future strong beat-and-raise story.

The company's core underwear business used to hold over 30% of the intimate market share in North America, but recently dropped to 20%, Nikic wrote. Winning back this lost market share — along with growing the company's PINK, swim, and activewear lines — could drive annual sales growth in the mid to high single-digit percentage range over the next few years.

Earnings per share could also reach $9.50 in five years, roughly double the company's current 2026 forecast of $4.45 to $4.70, according to Nikic.

Victoria's Secret stock tumbled nearly 13% in September following weaker-than-expected fiscal second quarter revenue. Jefferies analyst Corey Tarlowe previously said the stock reaction was "shaped more by expectations than reported results."

The price drop, however, didn't shake Nikic. He wrote the company was "one of the best-performing specialty retailers" in the first half of 2026.

Of the 15 analysts polled by FactSet who track Victoria's Secret, 53% recommend buying shares, while 40% have a Hold rating.

When Super joined Victoria's Secret, she also revived its fashion show. Traditionally held each October, the event has routinely generated massive buzz. Since its return, the stock has rallied every October, rising nearly 18% in 2024 and around 30% in 2025. The next fashion show is slated for this Sunday.

data.title: Wall Street fear gauge VIX surges to over four-month high
data.description:
The Cboe Volatility Index surged roughly 30% on Friday afternoon to trade above 21—reaching an over four-month high—amid circulating market rumors that a major hedge fund had collapsed.

After hovering near 16 throughout the morning session, the volatility gauge broke out sharply after midday, rising to an intraday high of 22.31 from a low of 15.73 before stabilizing near 21.43 at press time. The sudden afternoon spike marked a sharp departure from otherwise quiet VIX action.

Market commentators pointed to institutional distress as a potential catalyst for the volatility spike. CNBC options reporter Oliver Renick noted that trading conditions shifted dramatically within a 30-minute window as rumors circulated that a market participant was "getting blown out."

Jim Cramer echoed concerns over forced liquidations, observing that pressure in energy markets alongside "a big hedge fund blowing up" made Friday one of the worst trading days of the year.

Wall Street’s major market averages were markedly lower Friday, with the S&P 500 Index (SP500) down 1.2%, as technology stocks came under further pressure and oil prices extended gains. WTI crude climbed back above $100 per barrel, bringing its five-day increase to about 11%.

data.title: Asked for Diwali sweets, got flooded with costly COD orders: How influencer's viral post turned into delivery nightmare
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- A festive request made on social media has forced a Madurai-based content creator to leave his home after followers began sending a stream of unsolicited cash-on-delivery (COD) orders to his address.

Veeramani, who is known for his local slang and humorous online videos, had shared his residential address in West Anuppanadi, Madurai, in the hope that a follower would send him a box of sweets for Deepavali, according to PTI.

Instead, some followers allegedly used the address to place a series of COD orders in his name. Delivery personnel from e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart reportedly turned up at his residence with expensive electronic items, including washing machines, refrigerators, smartphones and televisions. One television order was reportedly valued at Rs.1.69 lakh.

Veeramani had neither placed the orders nor had the money to pay for them. He therefore could not accept the consignments or share the OTPs required to complete the deliveries.

The pranks reportedly extended beyond household goods. Some users also shared screenshots online claiming to have ordered heavy equipment, including JCB excavators and military tanks worth Rs.70 crore.

Food delivery executives from Swiggy and Zomato also allegedly arrived at his residence with orders placed by others. Distressed by the repeated deliveries, Veeramani posted a video appealing to his followers to stop the pranks. In the video, he said, "I am suffering a lot after requesting a sweet box. Please stop ordering. I am under severe pressure."

However, the deliveries reportedly continued despite his appeal.

When reporters and other social media influencers visited his residence in Anuppanadi, they found the house locked. Neighbours said Veeramani had left the premises after facing persistent harassment from delivery personnel arriving at different hours.

In his latest social media reels, the influencer said, "I am travelling. No one can find my address. Now, no one can control me now." Veeramani's current whereabouts remain unclear, while calls to the phone number listed publicly by him are reportedly being blocked.

When a prank COD order is refused at the doorstep, the shipment is generally classified as a Return to Origin (RTO), meaning it is sent back to the seller.

The seller can incur costs for both the forward delivery and the return journey, despite not completing the sale. According to Amazon Shipping India's guide on RTO, sellers typically bear the cost of both legs of the shipment and do not earn revenue from the refused order.

However, the seller does not necessarily have to absorb every charge. E-commerce platforms may reimburse certain fees depending on their fulfilment arrangements and policies. Amazon India's seller policy, for instance, provides reimbursements for specified charges on undelivered and customer-rejected shipments fulfilled through its Fulfilment by Amazon (FBA), Easy Ship and Seller Flex services.

These include referral fees, while eligible shipping, weight-handling, pick-and-pack and technology fees are also reimbursed depending on the fulfilment model.

The logistics partner is generally responsible for transporting the parcel to the customer and returning it to the seller if delivery is refused. The cost of these services is governed by its agreement with the seller or e-commerce platform.

Amazon Shipping India notes that an RTO can involve forward and reverse shipping charges, along with additional handling costs. Therefore, the courier company does not automatically bear the financial loss simply because the recipient refuses the parcel.

data.title: Kling AI Officially Launches Next-Generation Kling 4.0, Raising the Bar for Professional-Grade Video Models
data.description:
HONG KONG, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kuaishou Technology ("Kuaishou" or the "Company"; HKD Counter Stock Code: 01024 / RMB Counter Stock Code: 81024), a leading content community and social platform, today announced that Kling 4.0, the new-generation video generation model of Kling AI, officially launched on October 15.

Kling 4.0's upgrades center on three priorities: realism, control and professional quality. Designed for video creation scenarios featuring intense motion and complex camera movements, Kling 4.0 delivers breakthroughs in three areas: steadier large-scale motion, with smoother continuity in high-speed action and complex camera work; native generation of up to 30 seconds in a single pass, supporting long takes and continuous storytelling with a director's mindset throughout; and Omni Reference, which supports combinations of up to 15 reference assets and up to 10 keyframe inputs, helping creators turn a single idea into a complete work.

Working closely with professional creators to bring their projects to completion, particularly by delivering high-quality key shots, remains a key focus as the Kling model continues to evolve. Professional creators need more than the occasional stunning shot. They need to reliably deliver the key shots that define the quality of their work and bring generated footage into a complete production workflow. Kling AI believes that the value of technology lies not only in enabling content to be generated, but also in making the care behind every frame visible. Whether it's an emotionally charged close-up or a key shot that defines the look and feel of an entire work, every carefully crafted shot deserves to be done justice.

Mastering Both Drama and Action: Steadier Dynamic Motion and Complex Camera Work

Kling AI has long been known for film-grade dramatic scenes, with nuanced, lifelike portrayals of characters' emotions. Building on this strength, Kling 4.0 tackles one of the most common pain points in AI video, delivering more stable and fluid large-scale dynamic motion and complex camera movements. Whether it is high-speed movement and continuous action or sweeping camera movements such as tracking and orbit shots, Kling 4.0 maintains stable visuals and continuity, handling even the most intense large-scale scenes with ease and bringing AI video generation closer to true production-grade delivery.

On the audiovisual front, Kling 4.0 supports output of up to 10-bit HDR, delivering richer color depth and smoother transitions between light and shadow. In high-contrast scenes such as backlit shots, night scenes and neon-lit settings, it preserves greater detail in highlights and shadows, leaving more room for color grading in post-production. Kling 4.0 will also support 4K, 1080p and the 21:9 ultrawide format, further expanding the field of view and compositional possibilities for more immersive and cinematic visuals. For creators who carefully refine their work, these capabilities are more than spec upgrades. They are the foundation for giving key shots a higher level of polish and a more distinctive aesthetic.

For camera direction, Kling 4.0 supports native single-pass generation of up to 30 seconds, supporting long takes and continuous storytelling so that action, scene changes and emotional build-up can unfold in full. Its understanding of camera movements, including push-ins, pull-outs, pans, trucking shots, tracking shots and orbit shots, has been further enhanced, making changes in shot size and transitions smoother and more natural. The model also expands and enriches prompts with a director's eye, while prompt input length now reaches 8,000 tokens, allowing creative intent to be conveyed more fully and precisely.

Flexible Omni Reference: 15 Reference Assets, 10 Keyframes and Video Extension of up to Two Minutes

If 2025 marked the breakout year for AI video generation, 2026 has seen the industry boom. Competition in the field has also shifted from whether AI can generate video at all to whether it can do so reliably and with precise control.

Kling 4.0's upgraded Omni Reference supports flexible combinations of images, videos, subjects and voices in a single task, up to a total of 15 references, including up to 10 images, 5 videos and 7 subjects. These reference inputs work together to keep characters, actions, shots and audio closer to creators' intended results. Kling 4.0 supports a variety of image references, including subject images, three-view character sheets, grid images, storyboards and wireframes, and also allows creators to use video inputs to reference character performance, action, camera movement and narrative pacing. White-model videos and depth-map videos can also be used as references.

Creative recreation has also been upgraded. Creators can draw on the narrative pacing, shot composition and expressive style of a reference video and replace the products, characters and assets within it, quickly turning proven creative ideas into their own content and efficiently producing commercial videos for product advertising, viral social media content, fashion and beauty, consumer electronics and more.

With precise multi-keyframe control, Kling 4.0 supports up to 10 keyframe inputs, allowing creators to freely set key visual moments and precisely specify character states, scene changes and story beats so that content progresses naturally in the intended direction. In addition, the video extension feature will soon support multiple extensions of up to two minutes, giving actions, emotional build-up and multi-part storylines more room to unfold.

Powering Professional Content Creation and Taking Great Stories Global

AI is profoundly transforming production workflows in professional content creation such as film, television and advertising. As generative capabilities continue to improve, the value of AI video tools is shifting from boosting efficiency to enabling professional expression, not only increasing content production capacity but also helping creators consistently bring shots with higher aesthetic standards to life.

Kling 4.0 is also expanding into more creative use cases and genres, spanning film and television, short dramas, animation and advertising. At this summer's Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, which incorporated AI into its judging framework for the first time, two works created with Kling AI won Gold Lions, with AI-generated visuals increasingly taking on a central role in advertising storytelling.

In addition, with this major upgrade, Kling 4.0 has been integrated with Kling MCP and CLI, enabling creators to access Kling 4.0 capabilities such as Omni Reference and keyframe-to-video generation through AI agents. Beyond enhancing the user experience, Kling 4.0's model capabilities will soon be made available to enterprise customers and developers through API access, bringing advanced video generation to a wide range of industries.

About Kuaishou

Kuaishou is a leading content community and social platform in China and globally, committed to becoming the most customer-obsessed company in the world. Kuaishou uses its technological backbone, powered by cutting-edge AI technology, to continuously drive innovation and product enhancements that enrich its service offerings and application scenarios, creating exceptional customer value. Through short videos and live streams on Kuaishou's platform, users can share their lives, discover goods and services they need and showcase their talent. By partnering closely with content creators and businesses, Kuaishou provides technologies, products, and services that cater to diverse user needs across a broad spectrum of entertainment, online marketing services, e-commerce, local services, gaming, and much more.

Concerns the purported 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine has unraveled have also driven crude oil prices sharply higher.

data.title: US annual budget gap hits nearly $2 trillion, largest in 5 years
data.description:
Key points:
  • Debt-service outlays climb 12% to record $1.36 trillion, Treasury data shows
  • Net tariff receipts fall $22 billion after $145 billion of refunds
  • Fiscal 2026 deficit equals estimated 6.2% of GDP versus 5.8% in 2025

By Dan Burns

The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to nearly $2 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures showed on Friday.

Continued increases in spending for social benefits programs like Social Security and Medicare and a $48 billion jump in defense spending also factored into the increase.

The $1.99 trillion deficit for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, was up from $1.78 trillion in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third-largest annual deficit ever.

Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year.

Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago.

Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion.

Defense spending for the year rose by 6% to $917 billion. A US Treasury official said it was not clear how much of the increase could be attributed to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year.

The Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025.

For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

data.title: Hitachi Energy and Ansaldo Energia launch a strategic partnership to bring integrated power solutions to meet surging electricity demand

data.title: Alkermes reinstated Buy at Truist on narcolepsy opportunity
data.description:
Truist Securities on Friday reinstated its coverage of Alkermes with a Buy recommendation and a $55 per share target, citing the potential of its lead orexin development candidate, alixorexton, against narcolepsy, a sleeping disorder.

Analyst Alex Nackenoff argued that alixorexton has already shown a superior clinical profile against narcolepsy type 1, and its existing data is sufficiently strong in narcolepsy type 2 compared with oxybates.

However, according to Nackenoff, its proof-of-concept data expected from a Phase 2 trial for another neurological sleep disorder known as idiopathic hypersomnia represents the key near-term catalyst for the stock.

“The readout expected toward the end of 2026 presents an attractive risk/reward opportunity; we believe positive data could translate to potentially +20% on the upside with minimal downside risk if negative,” he added.

While Takeda is set to launch the first OX2R product branded as Orzeyful later this year, its opportunity is limited to NT1, according to Nackenoff. "Alixorexton has already demonstrated better efficacy vs. Orzeyful in NT1, and we feel the data is sufficiently strong in NT2 to deliver significant clinical benefit over oxybates,” the analyst added.

data.title: Companies Are Saying No to Tokenized Stocks-and Testing Wall Street's Crypto Push — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Joe Light

Crypto firms want to bring stocks to the blockchain, but a growing number of companies want no part of the new "tokenized securities venues."

OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto firm OKX and NYSE parent company Intercontinental Exchange, this week posted a notice disclosing that nine companies have objected to having their stocks traded on its proposed tokenized securities venue. That knocks out about 14% of the 63 stocks that the venture planned to include.

The opt-outs are part of a process established by the Securities and Exchange Commission to allow trading of tokenized stocks.

The SEC last month issued a so-called innovation exemption to let companies offer "tokenized" versions of traditional stocks. The new tokens would trade over blockchains, similar to cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, but would represent shares of real companies with the same governance and dividend rights.

However, as part of the exemption, the SEC required companies to post a public notice of their intent to launch a TSV and to give firms individually a chance to object to having their shares included on the new platform.

When OKXICE first posted its notice, it disclosed that Cerebras Systems had objected. As of Friday, the objectors also include AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon Communications, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group.

A spokeswoman for networking supplier Applied Optoelectronics said in a statement that the company objected because the framework is new and could have an uncertain impact on its stock's pricing, liquidity and volatility.

"At this stage, we don't see a clear benefit to AOI or our shareholders that justifies these uncertainties, and we will continue to evaluate the framework as it develops," said the spokeswoman, who also said the company did not want investors mistakenly believe that AOI had endorsed the offering.

The other eight objecting companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

OKX declined to comment. ICE did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In an interview with Barron's earlier this month, former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, who is now OKXICE co-chairman, said that objections from some companies were expected.

"There's going to be a transition period. It's so different. Some companies will jump in. Some will wait and see," Cuomo said.

Though it was never included on the OKXICE list, exchange operator Nasdaq in a FAQ explained why it had planned to opt its own shares out of any of the new securities venues. It said that in deciding whether to opt out, issuers should think about how the venues could "undermine transparent price discovery, fair access to market data, and the safeguards" that some traditional stock market regulations provide.

Company opt-outs might restrict some of the new securities venues, but other stock tokenization projects that don't rely on issuer cooperation are likely to continue apace. Nasdaq itself is among the firms participating in a project by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp. to tokenize stocks. SEC staff last year issued DTCC a "no-action" letter allowing it to proceed with its project without needing issuers' permission.

Unlike the OKXICE venture, which would allow retail investors to trade tokenized stocks, the DTCC service mostly involves what happens after a trade has occurred. Institutional investors can use the service to transform shares into tokens and then transfer them almost immediately on a 24/7 basis.

Write to Joe Light at joe.light@barrons.com

data.title: Chip Equipment Stocks Notch Historic Losing Streaks. AI Spending Fears Are Taking a Toll. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Shares of chip-equipment makers headed for historic losing streaks on Friday, dragged down by concerns about the hot pace of artificial-intelligence spending.

Lam Research fell 3.5% and KLA dropped 2.8%, putting both stocks on pace for their 10th consecutive daily decline. The streaks would be their longest on record. Their shares have plunged 22% and 17%, respectively, over that stretch, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Applied Materials declined 2.9%. The stock has fallen 22% over the last nine sessions, including Friday, marking its longest losing streak since May 2012.

These companies are big beneficiaries of the AI spending boom because they supply the machinery used to manufacture the advanced chips needed to power data centers and AI systems.

Investors have grown increasingly worried about the financing behind the AI boom, and whether the sky-high spending levels can continue. Those concerns were evident during this month's selloff in bonds issued by CoreWeave, the Nvidia-backed data-center operator.

Yields on some of CoreWeave's bonds surged to levels associated with financial distress, raising questions whether heavily indebted companies can sustain their massive infrastructure investments. Higher borrowing costs could force AI infrastructure developers, like CoreWeave, to scale back expansion plans — potentially weakening demand for advanced chips and manufacturing equipment needed to support the industry's growth.

Earlier this week, CoreWeave told Barron's its revenue backlog, which reached about $104 billion at the end of the second quarter, should more than support payments for all of its debt obligations.

Hotter-than-expected inflation data earlier this week added to pressure on chip-equipment stocks: The fear is the Federal Reserve might increase interest rates to rein in inflation and drive borrowing costs even higher.

The semiconductor industry is also grappling with growing competition from China, after Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies announced advances in next-generation memory technology. That offered a reminder that established chipmakers, including Micron and SK Hynix, could lose market share to Chinese rivals.

However, it's important to remember that demand remains strong for chip-equipment makers.

Applied Materials said earlier this week it expects industry spending on chipmaking equipment to grow faster through 2030 than the previous decade. The company stopped short of providing a spending forecast, citing uncertainty surrounding factory construction, supply chains, and infrastructure financing.

Dutch chip-equipment maker ASML offered another encouraging sign. In its third-quarter earnings report on Wednesday, the company said its customers were seeking to place orders for equipment as far ahead as 2030, with its demand to exceed production capacity in 2027 and 2028.

Even with the recent selloff, shares of Lam Research and KLA remain up about 59% and 41%, respectively, this year. Applied Materials is up 64%.

Write to Ty Roush at tyler.roush@barrons.com

data.title: Martin Marietta raised to Buy at D.A. Davidson after YTD underperformance
data.description:
Martin Marietta Materials climbed 1.1% in Friday's trading as D.A. Davidson upgraded the building materials company to Buy from Neutral with a $610 price target, saying the Lhoist North American acquisition lowers revenue and margin cyclicality, helping support valuation after theshares have underperformed YTD.

D.A. Davidson analyst Garik Shmois said he sees an attractive entry point for investors ahead of Q3 earnings and anticipated guidance for at least mid-single-digit to high-single-digit pricing in FY 2027, with upside potential as recent mix headwinds from NFS and Quikrete roll off.

High mid-single-digit to high-single-digit pricing should help price-cost spreads return to normal levels, assuming diesel prices remain flat and the company continues to execute on its plant automation and network optimization program, the analyst said.

Shmois also praised the combination with Lhoist North America that makes Martin Marietta the top U.S. producer of limestone products, saying it provides greater end-market diversity, optionality to capture value from construction aggregates currently sold by third parties at LNA sites, and a more stable margin profile through energy hedges.

data.title: Air Canada, United Airlines to expand Canada-US network with new summer routes
data.description:
Air Canada on Friday said it will launch new trans-border routes in partnership with United Airlines for summer 2027, expanding non-stop access to US destinations and enhancing connections across the country.

The carrier will launch services from Toronto to Louisville, Montreal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark during the season, while also increasing capacity on its Edmonton-San Francisco route by deploying larger Airbus aircraft.

Here are more details:

  • The expansion comes as Air Canada and United Airlines seek to deepen their presence in the Canada-US market through their joint business agreement, despite softer cross-border demand in recent months

  • The new routes support both business and leisure travel, while advancing Air Canada's strategy of connecting US passengers through its Canadian hubs to destinations in Europe and Asia, the Canadian airline said

  • United Airlines also announced a new seasonal service between Newark and St. John's, Newfoundland, and new flights from Denver to Ottawa and Quebec City, while increasing service on several existing Canada routes

  • The carriers have also agreed to renew and expand their trans-border joint business agreement, subject to regulatory approval from Canadian authorities, the airline said
